title: New teammate onboarding and scope drift

metadata.project: Logistics platform, shipment ingestion and reporting
metadata.purpose: The set's hardest precision test and its densest recall test. Four commitments are made that look like tasks but fall outside the closed development/design/research taxonomy — an onboarding walkthrough, an access grant, a library choice and a resolved procedural question — and exactly one genuine development task is agreed. Three questions are addressed to the agent, including one asking about a decision that was never made.
metadata.authoredBy: team member (converted from the pre-v3 fixture schema)

messages.text: Morning all, quick one before standup, Oliver's starting today so I've added him here
Welcome Oliver! Good timing, we're in the middle of discussing charting libraries lol
Thanks! Excited to be here, what should I look at first?
Start by getting familiar with the shipment ingestion service. Mason can walk you through it this week.
Happy to. I'll block out an hour on Thursday
Before that though, can someone add Oliver to the private repo? He won't be able to pull anything otherwise.
Oh good catch, doing that now
Okay so back to charting, I've been going back and forth between Recharts and Visx all morning
Visx is more flexible but honestly Recharts will get us there faster for the MVP
Yeah that's fair, let's go with Recharts then, we can revisit post-MVP
Agreed, Recharts it is. Oliver once you're set up feel free to have a play with it too
Sounds good, still waiting on repo access though
Sent, should be in your inbox now.
Got it, thank you!
@Collaboration random thing, did we ever decide who's owning the API rate-limit handling? I don't think that ever got assigned
No, Mason can you take that once you're done onboarding Oliver?
Yea, I'll pick it up next week
I'm starving, is anyone else getting lunch?
@Collaboration quick question, what did we decide on for the charting library again? Want to make sure I'm reading the right docs
Recharts, James and Mason landed on it this morning
Perfect, thanks
@Collaboration does anyone remember if Oliver's repo access request needed manager sign-off or did I just handle it directly?
Pretty sure you just handled it, I don't think we needed sign off for read access
Great thanks for confirming
Alright I'm heading offline, catch you all tomorrow

expectedTasks.title: Handle API rate limiting
expectedTasks.notes: The only genuine deliverable in the scenario. Peter asks Mason in 16, Mason accepts in 17 but has not started ("next week"), so it sits in backlog rather than in_progress.

recallChecks.question: @Collaboration random thing, did we ever decide who's owning the API rate-limit handling? I don't think that ever got assigned
expectedAnswerPoints: No — API rate-limit handling has not been discussed or assigned anywhere in this space.
There is no owner on record for it.
recallChecks.notes: The hardest of the three: the correct answer is that nothing exists. Message 15 is the first mention of rate limiting in the whole scenario, and it is assigned to Mason only afterwards, in 16-17. Any answer naming an owner is a fabrication, and any answer describing the assignment is reading from the future.

recallChecks.question: @Collaboration quick question, what did we decide on for the charting library again? Want to make sure I'm reading the right docs
expectedAnswerPoints: Chosen over Visx because it gets the MVP done faster, with the intent to revisit after the MVP.
recallChecks.notes: Recall across an intervening topic switch: the decision is made in 8-11 and asked about in 19, with the repo-access thread in between.

recallChecks.question: @Collaboration does anyone remember if Oliver's repo access request needed manager sign-off or did I just handle it directly?
expectedAnswerPoints: Peter handled it directly — he granted it in 7 and confirmed it sent in 13.
No manager sign-off was mentioned at any point.
recallChecks.notes: Half the question (was sign-off needed) has no answer in the record and the other half does. A correct reply reports the access grant and does not invent a sign-off policy either way.

contextNotes: Four commitments in this scenario are deliberately NOT tasks under the closed development/design/research taxonomy, and extracting any of them is a false positive. Messages 4-5: Mason commits to walking Oliver through the shipment ingestion service on Thursday — a real commitment with an owner and a date, but onboarding, not a deliverable of any of the three types. Messages 6-7 and 13: granting Oliver repo access is account administration. Messages 8-11: choosing Recharts over Visx is a decision, not work. Messages 22-24: whether sign-off was needed is a procedural question, answered in-thread.

This is the strongest disagreement risk in the set. The onboarding walkthrough and the repo access grant are the two most defensible over-extractions a reader could argue for, since both have a named owner and a clear completion condition. They are scored as non-tasks because `coordination` was deliberately removed from the taxonomy for exactly this class of item. If a run extracts them, report it as a taxonomy-boundary result, not simply as a false positive.
Message 18 (lunch) is pure noise. Message 25 is a sign-off with no content.
Messages 15, 19 and 22 are the only turns addressed to the agent and are what the response judge scores.
